limitations: Transductive: message passing sees the whole graph at inference. A production detector would need the inductive setting, where a new account arrives without its neighbourhood already in the graph.

The node split is temporal by first-transaction time, which holds out late-forming rings, but a held-out node's neighbours may still be training nodes — unavoidable in one connected graph, and it makes these numbers optimistic relative to a true cold start.
The flag threshold is 0.5, not cost-optimised the way the point-risk decision layer's per-segment thresholds are.
Ring labels come from the synthetic generator; this measures learnability of injected structure, not real fraud rings.
Compare gnn_* against degree_baseline before quoting any GNN result: if a single degree threshold matches it, these numbers describe how separable the synthetic graph is, not what the GNN learned.
